papers.title: Impact of hierarchical martensitic structure on deformation twinning in titanium alloys during additive manufacturing
papers.abstract: A fully hierarchical martensitic microstructure is the common feature of additively manufactured α-type Ti alloys due to the rapid cooling rate inherent to the fabrication process. However, how this hierarchy governs defect formation within α laths under cyclic thermal loadings remains poorly understood. Here, we present a systematic electron microscopy investigation of a Ti-6Al-4V fabricated by laser powder-bed fusion. The as-fabricated microstructure consists of fine α′ martensite organised into multilevel lath hierarchies inherited from prior β grains. Deformation twinning is found to be strongly dependent on the martensitic hierarchy. Two types of twins are identified based on their thickness and interactions with martensitic laths. Twins that link to the endpoints of fine martensitic plates laths, i.e., linked twins, are consistently thicker than non-linked twins within lath interiors. Such twin structures enhance the room temperature tensile performance, enabling a simultaneous improvement in tensile strength, ductility, and work-hardening capability. These results demonstrate that hierarchical martensite actively governs twin formation in additively manufactured Ti alloys, elucidating the microstructural origin of their superior mechanical properties and providing guidance for microstructural optimization.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接研究增材制造Ti-6Al-4V的层状马氏体组织对变形孪晶和拉伸性能的影响，完全符合L1方向。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover fatigue life or S-N curves; its mechanical focus is on tensile properties and work-hardening, not cyclic loading.

summary_zh.motivation: 揭示增材制造钛合金中层状马氏体结构对变形孪晶的影响机制。
summary_zh.method: 利用电子显微镜系统研究LPBF Ti-6Al-4V中不同尺度的孪晶及其与马氏体板条的相互作用。
summary_zh.result: 发现链接型孪晶比非链接型更厚，且孪晶结构能同时提升强度、塑性和加工硬化能力。
summary_zh.validation: 通过拉伸力学测试和微观结构表征验证。

summary_en.motivation: To understand how the hierarchical martensitic structure in additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V governs deformation twinning and its impact on mechanical properties.
summary_en.method: A systematic electron microscopy study was conducted on as-fabricated LPBF Ti-6Al-4V to identify twin types and their correlation with martensitic lath hierarchy.
summary_en.result: Linked twins at lath endpoints are thicker and contribute to simultaneous improvement in tensile strength, ductility, and work-hardening capability.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical tensile testing combined with detailed microstructural characterization.
